sources.document: Estudio hidrologico en la cuenca del rio Casma - Evaluacion de los recursos hidricos en las cuencas Casma, Culebras y Huarmey
admissible_claims: Cuenca Casma is N6 code 137596 and the study documents nine N7 units with exact names, codes and reported areas: 1375961 Bajo Casma, 1375962 Rio Sechin, 1375963 Medio Bajo Casma, 1375964 Rio Yautan, 1375965 Medio Casma, 1375966 Rio Vado, 1375967 Medio Alto Casma, 1375968 Rio Pira and 1375969 Alto Casma
the study documents the child-to-mainstem topology: Alto Casma/Chacchan, Pira and Vado feed the upper mainstem; Yautan joins Rio Grande; Sechin joins Rio Casma downstream
the study reports two auxiliary receiver units, Puente Quillo 137596A and Sector Tutuma 137596B, tied to hydrometric control points

the study states that INRENA digital cartography used in the GIS contained Pfafstetter N7 delineation and hydrographic layers, with IGN sheets 19g Casma, 19h Carhuaz, 20g Culebras and 20h Huaraz as base references
the 2007 surface-water inventory reports 626 quebradas distributed across the nine N7 units, providing a child-discovery QA target rather than activation evidence
historical hydrometric station names, watercourses, study-reported UTM locations and reliable periods may be used as documentary control context
forbidden_inferences: the PDF map image itself is an exact reusable vector geometry
manual tracing or visual digitization may be published as official N7 geometry without an independently reproducible georeferencing and QA contract
the 2007 reported areas or station values define present-day hydraulic capacity
historical monthly rainfall or flow statistics are IRFEN decision thresholds
the inventory count of a quebrada is evidence of activation or a negative control
